contract.name: verdigris-clean-machine-harness
contract.purpose: Define the deterministic stage contract a future disposable-host execution harness must satisfy before any Verdigris green counts as clean-machine evidence rather than cached developer success.
contract.audience: Implementers of the future clean-machine release harness (successor to TASK-0126 planning; consumes TASK-0092, TASK-0094, TASK-0099, TASK-0120 outcomes).

definitions.disposable_host: A machine provisioned from a declared base image, destroyed or reset after the run, with no inherited workspace state from any prior run.
definitions.clean_machine_run: A run on a disposable host whose workspace was freshly cloned at a pinned commit, whose caches started cold or carry complete provenance, and which produced the full evidence bundle defined by this contract.
definitions.cached_developer_success: Any green produced on a long-lived developer machine with warm caches, pre-built artifacts, or manually installed state. It is valid developer feedback and is NEVER clean-machine evidence.
definitions.stage: A named, ordered unit of harness work with pinned inputs, pinned commands, and a mandatory evidence record.
definitions.evidence_record: The machine-readable receipt a stage must emit; a stage without its evidence record is a failed stage regardless of exit code.
definitions.capsule: The loopback-only port range assigned to a lane (for example 6740-6759 for ox-pc-g).

invariants: INV-1: Every stage runs top-to-bottom in the declared order; no stage may be skipped, retried silently, or reordered without a new contract version.
INV-2: Every stage emits an evidence record with exit_code, command, base_commit, host identity, and UTC timestamps; missing evidence fails the run.
INV-3: A green is clean-machine evidence only when produced on a disposable host under a fresh checkout with cache provenance recorded; all other greens are cached developer success.
INV-4: All network binds are 127.0.0.1 only; all ports come from the lane capsule; port 6500 is owner-reserved and forbidden to every harness stage on every platform.
INV-5: The harness only terminates processes it started and tracked; it never signals peer processes.
INV-6: No stage installs system software, mutates CI configuration, or requires credentials beyond the read-only repository access needed for checkout.

INV-7: Determinism: identical inputs (base commit, lockfiles, toolchain pins, base image) must produce identical stage outcomes; any nondeterminism must be declared in the stage's nondeterminism_sources.

host_id.description: Unique identifier of the disposable host instance.

base_commit.description: Full 40-hex commit the workspace was checked out at.

log_ref.description: Reference to the captured raw log artifact.

cache_provenance.description: Required when the stage consumed or populated a cache; see cache stage.

clean_flags.description: Preconditions proven before the stage ran, e.g. FRESH_CHECKOUT, COLD_CACHE.

checkout.purpose: Produce a byte-deterministic workspace at one pinned commit with no inherited state.
checkout.determinism: Commit is pinned by full SHA; clone is shallow-free and verified against the pinned SHA; worktree is empty before clone.
preconditions: FRESH_VOLUME: workspace path absent or emptied before clone
PINNED_BASE: base_commit supplied by the harness caller, never resolved from a moving branch
evidence: resolved HEAD SHA equals pinned base_commit
git status --porcelain output is empty (DIRTY_BASE otherwise)
clone log artifact

toolchain.purpose: Prove the pinned toolchain exists and matches declared versions before anything builds.
toolchain.determinism: Versions are pinned as exact-or-floor pairs; the harness records observed versions and fails on mismatch.

cmake.policy: recorded; required only when native stage enabled

evidence: observed version for every required tool
explicit MISSING_TOOLCHAIN failure naming the absent tool and the pin it violated
nondeterminism_sources: host image tool drift; mitigated by pinning the base image digest per platform_matrix row

dependencies.purpose: Install dependencies exactly as locked, then prove the installed tree matches the lockfiles.
dependencies.determinism: Only lockfile-driven installs are allowed; npm install, yarn, pnpm ad-hoc installs are forbidden.
commands: dependency-tree fingerprint: hash of lockfile plus installed tree manifest, recorded as dependencies_fingerprint
evidence: npm ci exit code and log
dependencies_fingerprint recorded before and after install; equality proves no drift
DEPENDENCY_DRIFT failure names the fingerprint mismatch
nondeterminism_sources: registry-side package changes; mitigated by lockfile integrity hashes and optional offline mirror

cache.purpose: Make every cache use auditable so cached developer success can never masquerade as clean-machine proof.
cache.determinism: Cache keys are derived from content hashes (lockfile bytes, toolchain versions, source tree manifest), never from wall-clock or host name.
rules: CACHE-1: A clean-machine run must record, for every optional cache, either a cold-miss (populated during this run) or a hit with full provenance: key, source, content hash, and the producing run id.
CACHE-2: The first run on any new base image must be executed with all caches disabled; its artifacts seed the cache and its evidence is the only clean-machine baseline for that image.
CACHE-3: A cache hit without provenance is a CACHE_LEAK: the run is invalid as clean-machine evidence even if every stage exits zero.
CACHE-4: Developer workstations may use caches freely; their runs are labeled developer_local and are out of scope for acceptance evidence.
evidence: per-cache record: {name, key, cold_miss|hit, content_hash, producer_run_id?}
CACHE_LEAK failure names the cache and the missing provenance field

build.purpose: Compile browser and native targets from the proven-clean workspace.
build.determinism: Build commands are fixed; build IDs embed base commit; warnings are recorded, not suppressed.
commands: powershell -File native/build.ps1 (native target, no test flags)
evidence: exit code per command
artifact directory listing with sizes
NONZERO_STAGE failure names the stage, command, and captured log tail
nondeterminism_sources: compiler/linker timestamps embedded in binaries; mitigated by recording build IDs rather than byte-comparing binaries

tests.purpose: Run the deterministic test gates and record exact pass counts.
tests.determinism: Fixed test invocation, fixed ordering, no sharding unless declared; flaky retries forbidden (a retried pass is recorded as flaky, not green).
evidence: per-suite pass/fail counts stated numerically
exit code per command
NONZERO_STAGE failure includes failing test names and log tail
nondeterminism_sources: port collisions; mitigated by capsule allocation in the port stage

launch.purpose: Start the built server and client processes under harness ownership with recorded PIDs.
launch.determinism: Launch commands and flags are fixed; ports are allocated only from the lane capsule; readiness is polled, never slept blindly.
commands: record PID and command line per process into the run manifest
preconditions: CAPSULE_FREE: every allocated port verified free before launch
LOOPBACK_ONLY: bind address 127.0.0.1 asserted from process evidence, not from configuration intent
evidence: PID table: {process, pid, port, bind_address}
NON_LOOPBACK_BIND failure names process, port, and observed bind address
FORBIDDEN_PORT_6500 failure if any launch argument, config, or observed listener references port 6500

smoke.purpose: Prove the launched system serves the critical loop end-to-end.
smoke.determinism: One fixed smoke scenario per platform row; assertions are hard-fail (non-zero exit unless every on-screen/protocol assertion holds).
commands: browser lane: npm run smoke:browser (only where the platform row declares it)
evidence: scenario name, assertion count, pass count, exit code
screenshot or protocol transcript artifact per scenario
NONZERO_STAGE failure includes the failed assertion list
nondeterminism_sources: rendering timing on headless GPUs; mitigated by polling-based assertions with declared timeouts

process.purpose: Account for every process the run created and prove none leaked.
process.determinism: The harness tracks PIDs from launch; leak detection compares the tracked set against live processes after cleanup.
commands: enumerate listeners on capsule ports before and after the run
verify each tracked PID either exited cleanly or was terminated by the cleanup stage
rules: PROC-1: The harness may signal only PIDs recorded in its own run manifest.
PROC-2: Any tracked process still alive after cleanup is a LEAKED_PROCESS failure.
PROC-3: Untracked processes are never touched; they are reported, not killed.
evidence: before/after listener snapshots on the capsule range
per-PID exit status
LEAKED_PROCESS failure names pid, process, and held port

port.purpose: Enforce capsule-only, loopback-only port usage and the absolute ban on port 6500.
port.determinism: Port allocation is deterministic from the lane capsule; the forbidden set is fixed by contract, not configuration.
rules: PORT-2: All listening ports come from the lane capsule declared by the harness caller.
PORT-3: Port 6500 (owner live server) is forbidden in every config, command line, environment default, and observed listener, on every platform, for every lane.
PORT-4: The playtest default port 6510 may be used only by a full-suite run that holds the machine-wide serialization lease.
evidence: allocated port list with capsule bounds
observed listener table cross-checked against PORT-1/2/3
FORBIDDEN_PORT_6500 failure is always severity P0 and never waivable

cleanup.purpose: Return the host to a state safe to destroy: stop tracked processes, release capsule ports, remove run-local state.
cleanup.determinism: Cleanup order is fixed: terminate tracked processes, wait with timeout, then verify; host reset is the caller's responsibility and is recorded as host_disposition.
evidence: cleanup record per PID and per port
LEAKED_PROCESS failure if verification finds survivors

artifacts.purpose: Preserve durable, self-describing evidence for every run.

contents: stage evidence records in execution order
artifact file list with SHA-256 hashes

retention_rules: ART-1: Raw logs are captured verbatim; summaries never replace raw logs.
ART-2: Every artifact is hashed; the manifest carries the hashes.
ART-3: A run without a complete manifest is not evidence of anything.
ART-4: Debug-preserved workspaces must record their disposition and expiry.

clean_machine_decision.purpose: Single decision procedure separating clean-machine proof from cached developer success.
procedure: D-1: Was the host disposable and provisioned from a declared image? If no -> developer_local.
D-2: Was the workspace freshly cloned at a pinned commit with empty git status? If no -> DIRTY_BASE, invalid.
D-3: Did every cache record cold-miss or full provenance? If no -> CACHE_LEAK, invalid.
D-4: Did every stage emit a complete evidence record with exit code zero (or a declared, handled failure)? If no -> NONZERO_STAGE, invalid.

D-5: Did process/port verification prove no leaks, loopback-only binds, capsule-only ports, and zero contact with port 6500? If no -> LEAKED_PROCESS / NON_LOOPBACK_BIND / FORBIDDEN_PORT_6500, invalid.
D-6: Only when D-1 through D-5 all hold is the run labeled clean_machine_verified; anything else is developer_local evidence.
